title: CVE-2026-92387: never-ending loop via server response omission
explain: The real code shows the flaw the report describes.

summary: A malicious FTP/IMAP/POP3/SMTP server can cause libcurl's transfer timeout to be ignored and block other transfers on the same multi handle by never sending a final control-response line, leading to an unbounded loop in Curl_pp_readresp().

claims.text: Curl_pp_readresp() contains an unbounded do/while loop that reads up to 900 bytes and processes lines until the buffer is not full, without checking timeouts or invoking Curl_pgrsCheck() or Curl_pp_state_timeleft_ms() inside the loop.
claims.reasoning: The code confirms an unbounded outer loop that continues whenever a full 900-byte buffer is read. The inner loop processes all complete lines in the buffer but only exits the outer loop when endofresp() returns TRUE (final response line). No timeout or progress checks exist inside the loops.

citations.note: Outer do/while loop condition: while(gotbytes == sizeof(buffer)) at line 342
Inner do/while(1) loop processes lines until no newline found
endofresp callback checked; only breaks outer loop when it returns TRUE (line 325-326)
No call to Curl_timeleft_ms, Curl_pgrsCheck, or Curl_pp_state_timeleft_ms inside either loop

claims.text: The loop is inside Curl_pp_readresp() which is called from Curl_pp_statemach() after setting pp->response_time.
claims.reasoning: Curl_pp_statemach checks the timeout once at entry (line 70-76) then calls the protocol state machine. The FTP/IMAP/POP3/SMTP state machines call Curl_pp_readresp, which contains the unbounded loop.

citations.note: Curl_pp_statemach calls Curl_pp_state_timeleft_ms to get timeout_ms
Curl_pp_statemach invokes pp->statemachine (protocol-specific), which calls Curl_pp_readresp

claims.text: A server that never sends a final 3-digit reply code followed by a space (i.e., never satisfies LASTLINE()) keeps the loop reading and never returns.
claims.reasoning: Continuation lines like '220-...' have '-' at offset 3, not space, so LASTLINE() is false, ftp_endofresp returns FALSE, and the outer loop continues as long as the server keeps sending full 900-byte reads.

citations.note: LASTLINE macro: requires 3-digit code followed by space (line[3] == ' ')
ftp_endofresp returns TRUE only when LASTLINE() is satisfied
Outer loop breaks only when endofresp returns TRUE (line 325-326)

claims.text: The transfer timeout configured via CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS is never enforced for that transfer, and the same multi handle cannot service other transfers until the peer stops sending data.
claims.reasoning: The PoC demonstrates that CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS is not enforced (18x overrun) and the second transfer on the same multi handle is blocked until the malicious server stops flooding.

citations.note: Timeout checked only once in Curl_pp_statemach before statemachine call
Curl_pp_readresp loop has no timeout check
PoC shows a_done_at_ms=90005 vs configured 5000ms; b_done_at_ms=90005 vs ready at ~300ms

claims.text: The provided reproduce.sh script demonstrates the issue by running a malicious FTP server that floods non‑final 220‑... lines and shows that the timeout is not respected and other transfers are blocked.
claims.reasoning: The provided script builds and runs a working exploit demonstrating the timeout bypass and multi-handle blocking.

key_reasons: Curl_pp_readresp() contains an unbounded do/while loop (lines 252-342) that continues whenever pingpong_read returns a full 900-byte buffer, with no timeout or progress checks inside the loop.
The only timeout check occurs once in Curl_pp_statemach() (line 70-76) before entering the protocol state machine, which then calls Curl_pp_readresp().

FTP's ftp_endofresp() only returns TRUE for final response lines (3-digit code + space per LASTLINE macro). Continuation lines (220-...) never satisfy this, so a malicious server sending only continuation lines keeps the loop running indefinitely.

The PoC demonstrates CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 is bypassed (transfer takes 90s) and a second transfer on the same multi handle is blocked for the entire duration, even though its response was ready at ~300ms.

The project policy states: 'If the problem bypasses the regular counter-measures and it causes a never-ending transfer, it might be a security problem.' CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS is the documented counter-measure; this bug bypasses it.
reply: The report is well-grounded and the code confirms the unbounded loop in Curl_pp_readresp() lacks any timeout or progress checks. The PoC demonstrates CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS is bypassed and other transfers on the same multi handle are blocked. Per the project's 'Never-ending transfers' policy, this bypasses the documented counter-measure (CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS), making it a likely security issue. Suggested fix: bound the work per Curl_pp_readresp() call and call Curl_pgrsCheck/Curl_pp_state_timeleft_ms inside the loop.
